title: Doctor Dolittle
summary: This document provides a comprehensive overview of Doctor Dolittle, the central character of a series of children's books by Hugh Lofting beginning in 1920. The document covers the character's origins, including his first appearance in Lofting's illustrated letters to his children written from the trenches during World War I, and describes his role as a physician who can speak with animals, living in the fictional village of Puddleby-on-the-Marsh. It introduces the main human characters (Tommy Stubbins, Matthew Mugg) and his animal companions (Polynesia the parrot, Gub-Gub the pig, Jip the dog, and others). The document catalogs the complete series of books in publication order, highlighting notable works such as The Voyages of Doctor Dolittle, which won the Newbery Medal, along with special works like Gub Gub's Book and the Birthday Book. It also details the internal chronology of the stories, explaining how the reading order differs from publication order and noting chronological inconsistencies, particularly with Doctor Dolittle's Post Office. Additionally, the document lists numerous adaptations across various media, including radio, stage musicals, films (featuring actors like Rex Harrison, Eddie Murphy, and Robert Downey Jr.), animated series, and video games. Finally, it covers the character's influence in other languages and cultures, such as the Russian novel Doctor Aybolit and Norwegian adaptations, and notes that the character entered the public domain in the 1990s.
